_comment: Evidence registry. Source of truth for which prompts have been EXECUTED, as opposed to structurally reviewed. Add an entry only when a run happened and left a record; scripts/evidence_report.py validates every identifier against the catalog and every path against the filesystem, then generates _meta/evidence-levels.md.

_fields.identifier: prompt identifier, must exist in the catalog
_fields.title: human title
_fields.evaluator: who ran it, and whether they wrote the prompt
_fields.scope: what the run covered, in one line
_fields.result: outcome in one line, including defects found
_fields.limitations: what this run does not show

evaluations.title: Systematic Debugging
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: one synthetic fixture with a hidden mutable-default defect and a green test suite
evaluations.result: protocol completed end to end; three real prompt weaknesses found and fixed in v1.2.0
evaluations.limitations: single small fixture, author-evaluated, deterministic defect, familiar stack

evaluations.title: Conversational Debugging
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: tabletop walkthrough of a constructed fixture: a nightly sync failing with 'database is locked' at commit(), where the pasted code is innocent and a second uncommitted connection in unseen code holds the lock
evaluations.result: three real prompt defects found and fixed in v1.1.0: no instruction to find other holders of the same resource, a ledger unable to record findings outside the paste, and no rule for contradictions between the user's account and the evidence
evaluations.limitations: tabletop by the author, not a live user session; single fixture; database errors name their resource, which makes this lesson unusually easy to teach

evaluations.title: Chat Select: choosing the right prompt inside a conversation
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: six situations routed with the prompt as written, then each routing card scored against the generated TASKS.md index as external ground truth
evaluations.result: 4 of 6 cards named the prompt that TASKS.md assigns to the situation's task; two prompt defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 (no rule for a symptom that the index files under a different heading, and no requirement that the falsifier separate two prompts within a task), plus one index defect (background jobs were not reachable from the broken-now task)
evaluations.limitations: tabletop at a keyboard by the author, who wrote the situations and the questions; no live model and no second evaluator, so it tests the instrument and not compliance with it; six situations are a smoke test, not a benchmark

evaluations.title: Chat Code Review: reviewing a paste, with the limits stated
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded, and twice over: the target file was also written by the author)
evaluations.scope: one real file, scripts/check_prompt_contract.py, reviewed as written with the 'is this safe to merge' intent; the file computes a number the repository publishes
evaluations.result: six findings, two of them defects that inflated the library's own integration metric - a stem match satisfying a filename link, and substring matches such as 'planning' satisfying PLAN.md; 30 of 157 links had been scored as named on that basis. Prompt defects fixed in v1.1.0: no rule that a published number is the correctness question, and no rule to ask about the standard as well as the framework
evaluations.limitations: author-evaluated on both sides; one small Python file whose window happened to be complete, so the window claim was not tested; no second reader

evaluations.title: Chat Mode: adapting a prompt for a conversation
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: adapted GIT-P03 (history repair, risk class D when shared) for a chat window with no file or command access, then measured coverage of the source prompt's four prerequisite rows
evaluations.result: 4 of 4 prerequisite rows mapped; two real defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 - the workflow had no rule for a prerequisite that is a stop condition (the risk gate was left to the adapter to invent), and SESSION_LIMIT was declared but consumed by no step, so the state-block mitigation had no threshold
evaluations.limitations: one adapter, one target, one pass; the target was chosen because it breaks the rule, so it is a good test of the fix and a poor sample; no human ran the pasted commands

evaluations.title: Chat Design: a decision record from a conversation
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: a live tooling decision in this repository - merge the composition gate into the validator, or not - with measurements taken during the run (710/351/136 lines, 0.25/0.10/3.12 s, six documents naming the scripts)
evaluations.result: ADR produced with four options including do-nothing; three defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 - nothing required the status quo to be one of the options (the run nearly recommended extracting helpers that already existed), SCALE presumed a traffic volume that a code-structure decision does not have, and the ADR had no destination. The run also surfaced a repository defect: two CI workflows, one of which skipped the composition gate
evaluations.limitations: agent-chosen question on a repository the agent can see in full, which is the case the prompt was written against; no human filed the ADR

evaluations.title: Chat Handoff: carrying a long engagement between conversations
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: a 48-line packet for the 2.22.0 engagement, then a five-question reconstruction answered from the packet alone
evaluations.result: 5 of 5 questions answerable from the packet with no transcript; three defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 - the four labels had no way to express 'generated, true as of a date' (every count in a repository handoff is that), a fact contradicting the project's own docs had no label, and the required restatement had no template
evaluations.limitations: the cold read was not cold - the agent wrote the packet, the questions and the answers; the packet was never pasted into a different model; no secret appeared, so redaction was not exercised

evaluations.title: Prompt Forge: turning an intent into an executable prompt
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: compose a prompt for a gap the coverage matrix already names - requirements change control and traceability after baseline - with routing against four existing prompts and a self-score against the quality rubric
evaluations.result: a complete draft prompt (REQ-CHANGE-01), variables table, three test cases and a provenance line, self-scored 83/100; four defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 - the rubric band and the mandatory draft label were left contradictory, no rule existed for composing with no operator present, the self-score was emitted after the prompt, and the 70% overlap test had no method
evaluations.limitations: one intent, chosen by the author to match a known gap; the interview path ran in defaulting mode only; the generated prompt was not added to the library, so the gap is not closed

evaluations.title: Prompt Regression: measuring whether a prompt works
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: real execution of the generated REQ-CHANGE-01 against a synthetic git fixture at tag v1.4.0: three pre-registered cases (normal, no-approver, contractual refusal), two runs on the normal case, assertions checked by shell commands
evaluations.result: all three decisions correct and no baseline file edited; one defect found in the prompt under test (a change that weakens a security control was accepted with only a product approver, and the safeguard appeared in 1 of 2 runs of identical input); four defects found in GEN-P02 and fixed in v1.1.0 - the 'fresh session' requirement had no isolation procedure and could be claimed without being met, no budget rule for which case gets the second run, no trace format, and a collision with the library's own evidence convention; v0.2.0 retested with three runs (two normal, one adversarial): 3 of 3 name the control owner and block on the missing signature, so the 1-of-2 instability does not recur; a residual vocabulary ambiguity (accepted-with-condition vs deferred) is recorded and unresolved
evaluations.limitations: no isolation: every run shared one context, so the instability may be an artifact of that; n=1 on two of three cases; rubric score self-assessed

evaluations.title: Repository State & Safety Check
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: real execution on a purpose-built git fixture: one branch, one commit that exists nowhere else, an untracked file, no remote
evaluations.result: artifact produced and every safety assertion held (in-progress operation correctly none, unpushed commit identified, backup branch recorded, recommendation correct); two defects fixed in v1.1.0 - the recommended git stash create snapshot is unreachable and expires silently, and the artifact's .git-ops location was never specified as local-only
evaluations.limitations: synthetic five-file fixture with one author; no remote, so the shared-history branch of the assessment was untested

evaluations.title: Conflict Resolution
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: real merge conflict resolved as stage 2 of the git-operations system, consuming GIT-P01's STATE.md: a rename on one side, a capability plus config change on the other, and a lockfile both sides touched
evaluations.result: both intents preserved (grep for the old symbol empty, tests pass, no markers, history unrewritten) and the direction-of-ours rule worked; one High defect found and fixed in v1.1.0 - the regenerate-generated-files rule keys on conflict type, so a lockfile git auto-merged in silence is never checked
evaluations.limitations: two stages of a five-stage system, not an end-to-end run; no package manager, so the repaired rule could not be tested against a real lockfile; a merge was run, not a rebase, where the direction rule matters most

evaluations.title: History Repair
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: real squash-and-reword of three unpublished commits on a local branch with no remote, backed up first
evaluations.result: tree hash identical before and after (d5143b7d), 3 commits reduced to 1, backup branch preserved the original, other refs untouched, tests pass; no prompt defect found - the stage's classify/backup/mapping/verify sequence is what made the result checkable
evaluations.limitations: local-only rewrite with no remote, so the shared-history authorisation path (risk class D) was not exercised; single-branch, three-commit case

evaluations.title: Recovery: getting lost work back
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: a commit made unreachable with git reset --hard HEAD~1, located through the reflog and restored
evaluations.result: content restored with an identical tree hash (6477a541), other refs untouched, no fsck needed; no prompt defect found
evaluations.limitations: recovery happened minutes later, well inside reflog expiry, which is the condition the prompt warns about; no expired-reflog or gc-pruned case

evaluations.title: Hygiene & Collaboration Conventions
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: conventions produced for a real fixture with one inferred author, no remote, no tags, and a committed bytecode artefact
evaluations.result: trunk-with-tags model, squash default, and every rule's enforcement recorded as convention-only where nothing enforces it; two defects fixed in v1.1.0 - the generated-code rule never told the operator to scan what is committed (a .pyc had survived four stages), and an unobservable CI fact had no 'not observable' option
evaluations.limitations: no hosted remote, so protection rules and red-build history were unobservable by construction; the .gitignore recommendation was not applied, to preserve the artefacts other stages verified

evaluations.title: Review Context & Goals
evaluations.scope: set up a review of the tooling diff v2.21.1..main (12 files, +1794/-80): stated intent, scope metrics, change type, three risk areas named before the diff was read, four hypotheses and a sampling depth
evaluations.result: all eight verification checks pass; the risk-first ordering changed what was looked for - the runner as single point of failure was named as a hypothesis before the code was read, and it was where the defect was
evaluations.limitations: agent-authored target and agent grader; one review, one diff
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author, who also wrote the code under review (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Change Understanding
evaluations.scope: read the diff by module, reconcile against the stated intent, and carry discrepancies forward as hypotheses
evaluations.result: three discrepancies carried to P03 (runner has no test; the runner writes to the tree; nothing proves a self-test can fail); the third did not survive verification, which was recorded rather than quietly dropped
evaluations.limitations: 500 of 1794 lines sampled, not read
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author, who also wrote the code under review (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Structured Review
evaluations.scope: findings for the tooling diff, each demonstrated before being recorded
evaluations.result: one High (a failing validator run left _meta/CATALOG.md rewritten in the working tree, so the gate dirtied the tree exactly when it failed), one Medium (the runner was the only script with no test), two Low; all four fixed, and the High was reproduced before and after the fix
evaluations.limitations: reviewer wrote the code being reviewed; three of six stages ran, so not an end-to-end system run
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author, who also wrote the code under review (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Context & Goals
evaluations.scope: set the goals for this repository's own gate suite: the number that matters is the wall-clock time of `scripts/check_all.py`, which every contributor runs before pushing
evaluations.result: one measurable goal with a source (the gate suite's own runtime), three critical paths and a non-goals list; the goal was written before any measurement, which is what made the later 25% claim checkable
evaluations.limitations: one system, one goal; the traffic analogy does not transfer to a local gate runner
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Measurement Setup
evaluations.scope: build a three-run median harness over the gate suite and a per-gate breakdown, and record the environment
evaluations.result: suite median 3.40 s (3.34-3.67), per-gate breakdown captured for 15 gates; the spread across three runs was 9.7%, just inside the prompt's own 10% soundness rule, which the report had to state rather than hide
evaluations.limitations: single machine, single workload; no CI runner to compare against because Actions is blocked by billing
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Analysis
evaluations.scope: attribute the 3.40 s across gates and sweep one dimension
evaluations.result: two gates ran the same detector over the same corpus; together they owned 54% of gate time (1.74 s of 3.20 s), and the remaining 13 gates totalled 1.46 s
evaluations.limitations: attribution is per-process wall clock, so interpreter startup is included in every gate
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Bottleneck Identification
evaluations.scope: confirm the duplicate-detector cost by ablation and rank the rest with ceilings
evaluations.result: ablation confirmed: running the detector once instead of twice removed 0.84 s. A second candidate, the O(n^2) shingle comparison, was measured at 0.52 s and cut to 0.02 s by an inverted index, verified against 200 sampled pairs with zero mismatches
evaluations.limitations: the ceiling estimate assumed the two gates were redundant, which the ablation then had to prove rather than assume
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Optimization Design
evaluations.scope: choose between merging the two gates and rewriting the detector's core loop
evaluations.result: both were planned, and the plan required byte-identical output before either could be kept: every metric's report and the JSON were diffed against the pre-change version
evaluations.limitations: the prediction was written before the change and was off by 0.26 s on the first attempt, which is recorded rather than revised
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Implementation & Validation
evaluations.scope: implement the multi-metric pass, the inverted index, and the merged gate; then measure and verify correctness
evaluations.result: suite median 3.40 s to 2.56 s (-25%); all four metric reports and the JSON output byte-identical to the pre-change version; 112 self-test cases pass, up from 106, with 4 new cases for the failure rule and 2 for the scan
evaluations.limitations: one machine, one corpus; the correctness evidence is the repository's own suite plus a diff of the detector's output, not an independent measurement
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Performance Orchestrator
evaluations.scope: coordinate the six stages against one target and record the gates between them
evaluations.result: all six stages ran in order and each gate passed; the orchestrator's own rule stopped the chain once the second optimisation reached the noise floor of the harness
evaluations.limitations: a single run of the sequence; the orchestrator was not exercised on a blocked stage
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)

evaluations.title: Context & Package Understanding
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: executed against the real package sindresorhus/p-map at v7.1.1, a repository with no changelog, no lockfile, a compound test script and a published surface smaller than the tree
evaluations.result: four defects in v1.0.0, three of them High: bundled scripts were never decomposed, the shipped surface was never recorded although a later stage validates it, and one verification item was unachievable when the versioning policy is unstated with no honest route for that. v1.1.0 fixes all four and the retest passes five of six checks with the sixth recorded as partial
evaluations.limitations: one target, npm only, chosen and graded by the prompt's author; stages P02-P08 not run, so the system is partially tested end to end

evaluations.title: Data Assessment
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded; the fixture was built by the author who knew where the traps were)
evaluations.scope: run against a purpose-built churn fixture of 1,200 account-months with three planted leakage paths, one of them statistically perfect but structurally innocent, and a random-split defect
evaluations.result: v1.0.0 missed the statistically perfect leak because the procedure was schema-first, and had no honest state for a check with no pipeline to hold it. v1.1.0 adds a label-determinism scan (categorical levels at 0 or 100 percent, numeric columns by threshold separation) and a 'pending - no pipeline yet' state; the retest found all four planted defects and labelled every mitigation pending rather than prevented
evaluations.limitations: one fixture, one domain, built by the prompt author; the other seven stages of the family remain unexecuted, so the system is partially tested end to end; the fixture is not committed
